messages.author: d66aa3feb509150a
messages.subject: pass data directly to javascript?
parts:
Hello, I'm trying to see how to pass R data more directly to javascript. In particular I'd like to be able to pass R objects directly to a D3 script that then takes those data and does the rendering work. 

I'm hoping I'm missing something obvious, since working with browser code is pretty new to me. 

I have this trivial server.R: 

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  ## reactive data
  data <- reactive({
      n <- input$n
      sample(n, n/10)
  })

  # Generate an HTML table view of the data
  output$table <- renderTable({
    data.frame(x= data())
  })

})



and this HTML, following the "Build your entire UI with HTML" topic:

http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/html-ui.html 

<html>

<head>
  <script src="shared/jquery.js" type="text/javascript"></script>
  <script src="shared/shiny.js" type="text/javascript"></script>
  <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="shared/shiny.css"/> 
</head>

<body>
  <h1>HTML UI</h1>
  <p>
    <label>Number of observations:</label><br /> 
    <input type="number" name="n" value="50" min="1" max="1000" />
  </p>
   <div id="table" class="shiny-html-output"></div>
</body>
</html>

I know I can obtain the "table" element with a D3 script like this (even though there's no practical use of this as it stands), but I'd like to avoid using shiny to render the data, and just pass the raw data to javascript (presumably via RJSONIO::toJSON): 

<script src="http://d3js.org/d3.v3.min.js" charset="utf-8"></script> 
<script>
var dat = d3.select("#table"); 
console.log(dat);
</script>

I think I'm missing something pretty obvious, so hoping someone could explain how or point to an example. 

Cheers, Mike.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: pass data directly to javascript?
parts:
You definitely want to use the new htmlwidgets package that we've been co-developing with Ramnath. It's designed specifically for this sort of thing.

https://github.com/ramnathv/htmlwidgets

htmlwidgets makes it easy(-ish) to create an R package that brings a JavaScript library into R-land. When you create a widget library on top of htmlwidgets, it works not only in Shiny but also in R Markdown documents and even in RStudio (when you print such a widget at the R console it shows up in a viewing pane right in the IDE).

Here's an example of a D3 widget that's built on top of htmlwidgets:

http://christophergandrud.github.io/networkD3/
https://github.com/christophergandrud/networkD3
